Following the release of Xcode 27.1 beta 1 last week, Bitrig has added support for building and testing iPhone Duo apps, along with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device at will. Here are the details.

Bitrig now lets users interact with the iPhone Duo in 3D

Bitrig originally launched as a simple vibe-coding app that lets users turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps, running directly inside the Bitrig main app on iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded significantly, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps via TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, following Apple's release of Xcode 27.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing iPhone Duo apps, Bitrig rolled out its own iPhone Duo support and reimagined the simulator in a more interactive way.

Here's a look at what the update brings from Bitrig co-founder and CEO Kyle Macomber:

Try out every pose. The iPhone Duo can sit flat on a desk like a laptop, or stand up like a tent on a nightstand. Opened, folded, or half-folded, portrait or landscape — your app needs to adapt. Bitrig's 3D simulator lets you grab, fold, and rotate it, watching your app respond in real time. React to the hinge. Use onHingeChange to drive interactions and effects as the phone folds — like Apple's unfold effect that makes the outer screen feel like a window into the inner one. Read hinge data live as you open and close the device in the built-in simulator. Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to lay out media content on the top half and controls on the bottom half when the iPhone Duo is sitting flat on a desk. Support landscape orientation so users can use your app with the outer screen standing tall. Use both screens at once. Add CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer screen so the person facing the camera sees something useful.

Macomber also noted: "Bitrig helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start prepping your apps for iPhone Duo on the beta first, then switch back to Xcode 27 anytime to build and ship updates."
